- toSum_src and toSum_tgt: the same three-line `show … ; rw [Equiv.symm_apply_apply]`. This is routine unfolding, so a shared lemma is not worth it.
- The inl/inl and inr/inr cases of sumEnds_unique (about 13 lines each): both unpack the Sigma equality, subst, apply Sum.inl_injective or Sum.inr_injective, and use the ∃! hypothesis. The only reasoning they share is `ExistsUnique.unique` plus HEq/Sigma plumbing. A helper would mostly move the duplicated branches inside it, because the two cases use different uniqueness fields (existsUnique_xs_eq vs existsUnique_xt_eq) and different projections. The two mixed cases differ only by symmetry and take about three lines each.
- In `solution`, hdom, hres and hpm each call `forall_teleChart_iff` with ig and ss branches that are near-identical. The branches are one-line projections of the hypotheses, so this is a thin pattern.
- The final two existence blocks both build `arithmeticGalois (F0 q M') τ` with `(hS _).mpr ⟨τ, hτI, hτ1, rfl⟩`. That is a one-line repetition.
None of these is a nontrivial mathematical argument repeated in two proofs. Any refactor would need a heavily parameterised helper with little gain, so I report no finding. I could not run Lean to test any candidate refactor.
